ontology: congenital vitamin k-dependent coagulation factors deficiency
rationale: The two candidates are effectively near-clones on endpoint fidelity (identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported), study archetype (same UKB portability paper), training cohort/size, covariates, evaluation ancestry mix, and validation N. Their only reported performance signal is partial-r and it is indistinguishable (0.0563 vs 0.0562), with no PRS-only AUC/R2 or effect sizes to separate them. In this tie, the most defensible differentiator is model structure: PGS002034 uses genome-wide shrinkage (LDpred2) with far broader variant coverage (32,552 vs 45), which is generally more likely to capture polygenic signal and thus rank higher in an external benchmark when all other evidence is equal. Pairwise judgment is consistent with this and there is no countervailing metric evidence favoring PGS001826.

All three candidates are near-clones from the same UKB pan-trait snpnet framework with identical basic covariates and similar ancestry/validation context, so the most defensible differentiators are endpoint fidelity and directly comparable PRS-only metrics. PGS001262 uses a straightforward doctor-diagnosed angina phenotype (closest to a generic angina pectoris target, avoiding the time-to-event framing of PGS001261) and it has the strongest PRS-only performance among the shortlist (PGS-only AUROC 0.58683; PGS-only R2 0.01304), edging both PGS001261 and PGS001260. The pairwise judgments are internally consistent in selecting PGS001262 over each alternative with grounded metric-and-endpoint reasoning, and the PRS-only R2 remains plausible under the provided heritability ceiling (no inflation red flag).

PGS000327 has the cleanest endpoint fidelity to the target: trait_reported, trait_efo, and especially phenotyping_reported are all explicitly autism spectrum disorder, whereas PGS002790 has an explicit phenotype mismatch ("Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)") that raises strong endpoint-incoherence/leakage risk despite ASD label fields. On performance evidence, PGS000327 shows a materially stronger signal (OR per SD 1.33 with tight CI and higher reported R²=0.0245) than PGS002790’s modest partial R²=0.00546 and no effect-size support; covariates for PGS000327 are basic (PCs, genotyping wave) and comparable. Although PGS002790 uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (SDPR) with many variants, that structural advantage is outweighed by the phenotype inconsistency and weaker/less interpretable performance package. The pairwise judgment is internally consistent with these multi-field differences, so PGS000327 is the most likely hidden-benchmark #1.

Both candidates are endpoint-identical near-clones from the same UKB portability study (same trait/phenotyping, same training cohort and N, same covariates, same evaluation ancestry mix and validation N), and neither provides PRS-only AUROC/R² to separate them cleanly. In this tie-like setting, the best available comparable metric is the selected European validation partial correlation, where PGS002042 is higher (partial-r 0.0471 vs 0.0384). This is reinforced by a structural edge: PGS002042 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far more variants (59,944 vs 38), which is generally favorable when all other fields are effectively matched. The pairwise judgment is consistent with these multi-field differences, so PGS002042 is the best-supported pick for hidden-benchmark top rank.

PGS001033 is the strongest pick for a hidden external benchmark on the target trait because it has the best endpoint alignment (trait_efo exactly matches the target “blood coagulation disease”, with a coherent coagulation-defects phenotype, albeit time-to-event) and it is the only candidate with directly PRS-comparable discrimination reported (PGS-only AUROC=0.634 and PGS-only R²=0.0578). In contrast, PGS002034 and PGS001826 target a narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency subtype and provide only a small partial correlation (~0.056) without PRS-only AUROC/R², making their predictive evidence less comparable for ranking. The pairwise judgments are internally consistent (PGS001033 beats both alternatives), so following that evidence yields PGS001033 as most likely to rank #1 externally, with moderate confidence due to the framework/sparse-model origin and the time-to-event endpoint.

Across the shortlist, PGS001135 is the only candidate with directly PRS-comparable discrimination reported for an arthritis endpoint (PGS-only AUROC=0.539 and PGS-only R²=0.00291), with basic covariates disclosed and a selected European validation record; its PRS-only R² is also plausibly below the provided heritability ceiling, making the metric interpretable. The two 2024 “M13 (Other arthritis)” candidates (PGS004547/PGS004477) are near-clones in endpoint and cohort context and show only modest per-SD ORs (1.26 vs 1.20) with unknown covariates and no AUC/R², leaving their standalone PRS strength less well-supported for a hidden benchmark. Given the pairwise judgments are internally consistent (PGS001135 beats both siblings; PGS004547 beats PGS004477 only within their near-clone pair), the best-supported overall choice for likely top external benchmark rank is PGS001135, albeit with moderate confidence due to its pan-trait UKB framework archetype.

PGS003428 has the strongest overall evidence package for hidden-benchmark top performance given the available fields: it is endpoint-faithful (incident cervical cancer; EFO cervical carcinoma), comes from a cervical-phenotype GWAS meta-analysis explicitly aimed at risk stratification, and uses a genome-wide shrinkage construction (LDpred) with ~2.9M variants—structurally more likely to capture polygenic signal than the 10-variant GWAS-hit scores (PGS000073/PGS000784). The higher AUROC/C-index reported for PGS000073/PGS000784 is full-model and paired with a much heavier covariate bundle, so it is not cleanly attributable to the PRS and is not comparable to PGS003428’s lighter covariate context. Between the near-clone 10-variant siblings, PGS000073 is better-supported than the inverse-weight derivative PGS000784, but both remain structurally weaker than the disease-focused genome-wide LDpred score. Pairwise judgments are internally consistent and select PGS003428 over both alternatives, supporting this choice.

PGS004951 has the strongest overall evidence package for hidden external-benchmark top rank because it reports PRS-comparable performance directly attributable to the score (univariate PRS-only AUC=0.67 with CI; delta PRS/residual liability-scale R²=0.101), whereas PGS004862/PGS004861 only provide full-model AUROC/R² with demographic covariates, which is explicitly non-substitutable for PRS-only performance and may be covariate-driven. Endpoint fidelity is at least as good (phenotyping_reported is explicitly “Clinical dilated cardiomyopathy”), evaluation is EUR like the others, and its per-SD effect size is also strongest (OR 1.93 vs 1.76/1.56), supporting better discrimination. The smaller validation N for PGS004951 is a weak negative tie-break and does not outweigh the clearer PRS-isolated metrics plus stronger effect-size evidence. Pairwise judgments are internally consistent and unanimously select PGS004951 over both alternatives, aligning with these multi-field advantages.

All three candidates are endpoint-faithful to celiac disease, but none provides a clean PRS-only AUROC/R2, so we must lean on study archetype + structural signals rather than treating reported full-model metrics as directly comparable PRS performance. The pairwise judgments are internally consistent (PGS000040 beats both others), and their rationales rely on multiple grounded fields (disease-focused vs framework archetype; method/variant count; limited interpretability of partial-r). Between the two disease-focused models, PGS000040 has stronger structural support for top external-benchmark rank: it uses a higher-capacity disease-specific statistical learning approach (SparSNP) with more variants (228 vs 53) and reports a slightly higher AUROC (0.90 vs 0.879), acknowledging both are likely full-model. PGS002067 is penalized as a pan-trait portability-framework score with only a modest partial correlation and no discrimination metric, making it less likely to be the hidden benchmark #1 when a disease-focused alternative exists. Overall, PGS000040 has the best-supported whole-record profile for external performance among the shortlist.

PGS005170 has the strongest overall evidence package for ranking #1 on an external dementia benchmark: it is an explicit all-cause dementia score with incident all-cause dementia phenotyping (tight endpoint fidelity), built as an integrative/ensemble PRS combining multiple genome-wide PRS constructions (LDpred2/PRS-CS/C+T) with very large variant coverage (1.32M), and it has multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR) supporting robustness/transportability. Competing candidates either have weaker endpoint mapping (PGS000823 is Alzheimer’s-disease–labeled and is a sparse 23-variant GWAS-hits score with only a tertile HR and no discrimination metrics) or are more likely to be internally optimized to a single-biobank context with non-comparable full-model metrics (PGS004281: UKB-only, 110 variants, only full-model AUROC/pseudo-R2 without PRS-only isolation). The pairwise judgments are cyclic, but two of three comparisons favor PGS005170 and their rationales align with the most reliable selection signals (endpoint fidelity + structural robustness + broader evaluation), so PGS005170 is the best-supported choice despite lacking PRS-only AUC/R2.

PGS002738 has the strongest endpoint fidelity to the target trait (alcohol dependence): its trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are explicitly Alcohol use disorder and its trait_efo maps directly to alcohol dependence, whereas PGS000201/PGS000202 are labeled “Problematic alcohol use” with a more proxy-like trait_efo (“alcohol dependence measurement”) despite DSM-5 criteria-count wording. Across the pairwise judgments, PGS002738 consistently beats both siblings with grounded rationales (phenotype alignment plus stronger available effect evidence). While none of the candidates provides clean PRS-only AUC/R2, PGS002738 reports a meaningful risk-stratification signal (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96), which is stronger and more directly interpretable for discrimination than the small incremental ΔR² values reported for PGS000201/PGS000202. Transportability/study context is also at least as supportive (MVP+UKB development; similar EUR-only evaluation; comparable validation N), with no clear packaging/leakage red flags beyond unknown covariates. Given the consistent pairwise wins and the combination of better phenotype alignment plus stronger effect-size evidence, PGS002738 is the most likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark.

All three candidates are endpoint-faithful near-clones (same basal cell carcinoma trait/EFO/phenotyping, same publication family and release date, same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL context, same training cohort and N, same basic covariates, same validation N) and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we must rely on within-family tie-breaks from the same evaluation context. The pairwise judgments are internally consistent (PGS000454 beats both PGS000452 and PGS000456), and the record-level metrics support that: PGS000454 has the highest full-model Nagelkerke R² (0.0489 vs 0.0487 vs 0.0456), matches the top AUROC tier (0.632 vs 0.632 vs 0.630), and has the strongest per-SD OR among the three (1.661 vs 1.663 vs 1.633; essentially tied with PGS000452 but clearly above PGS000456). While top-1% OR is slightly higher for PGS000456, the broader discrimination/effect-size package in the shared setting favors PGS000454 as most likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark.

PGS004254 is the most likely #1 external-benchmark performer because it is endpoint-faithful to generic Crohn’s disease (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both direct CD) and comes from a disease-focused study archetype using a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2-auto) with very broad variant coverage (744,682), which is structurally more consistent with strong external PRS performance than the very sparse snpnet scores from the pan-trait UKB “across 813 traits” framework. Although PGS004254 lacks PRS-only AUROC/R² (its AUROC=0.72 is full-model and not directly comparable), it provides supportive PRS-discrimination evidence via a strong per-SD effect size (OR 2.18). The two snpnet candidates (PGS001331, PGS001330) have clean PRS-only metrics but are near-clone sparse framework models with modest PRS-only AUROC (~0.58) and low R² (~0.006–0.007), and PGS001330 additionally has a time-to-event phenotype mismatch. The pairwise judgments are internally consistent (PGS004254 beats both others), so the overall evidence favors PGS004254 despite missing PRS-only AUC/R².

The pairwise judgments form a low-confidence cycle (002786 > 002788, 002788 > 002787, 002787 > 002786), so I re-rank from the records. All three are near-clones (same paper, SDPR, ~935–949k variants, EUR-only GWAS/EVAL, basic covariates age+PCs, no PRS-only AUC/R²; only tiny partial R² values reported in non-disease phenotyping contexts), so the most reliable differentiator is endpoint/trait alignment to the target. PGS002786 is the only candidate whose trait_reported/trait_efo are the generic target (“Bipolar disorder”), whereas PGS002787 and PGS002788 are explicitly subtype-specific (bipolar I / bipolar II), which is a mismatch risk for a hidden benchmark defined on broad bipolar disorder. The slightly higher partial R² for PGS002788 is weak evidence here because the reported phenotyping_reported endpoints differ across candidates and are not direct bipolar diagnosis endpoints, making those partial R² values hard to compare as PRS-quality signals. Given the near-tie on all structural/transportability fields and the non-comparable performance reporting, the safest pick for #1 on an external bipolar-disorder benchmark is the broad, directly matched bipolar-disorder score: PGS002786.

PGS005254 has the cleanest overall evidence package for ranking #1 on an external benchmark for the target disease endpoint. It is directly aligned to incident aortic stenosis (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all match), and its reported PRS association (HR=1.64 with CI) is estimated under a relatively basic covariate set (age, age^2, sex, PCs), making the effect size more comparable to standalone PRS signal than a heavily clinically adjusted model. PGS005252 is also endpoint-faithful and shows a larger HR (1.92), but its evaluation context includes many clinical comorbidities and risk factors and the only discrimination metric shown is a full-model C-index (0.87), which is likely covariate-inflated and not a reliable proxy for PRS-only performance; it also lacks an uncertainty interval for the HR. PGS005255 is a weaker match because it is labeled as a related quantitative trait (“Mean pressure gradient”) despite sharing an incident AS phenotyping line, and it has a smaller HR (1.53) than PGS005254 in an otherwise near-clone setting. The pairwise judgments are internally consistent in selecting PGS005254 over both alternatives, and the record-level fields support that choice.

Pairwise judgments are internally consistent (PGS004913 beats both alternatives; no cycle), and the rationales rely on multiple grounded fields (endpoint fidelity, covariates clarity, study archetype, and PRS-relevant effect evidence), so we follow that winner. All three candidates map to the same EFO, but PGS004913 has the cleanest disease-focused endpoint framing (alcohol-associated cirrhosis among heavy drinkers) with explicit basic covariates (age/sex/PCs) and PRS-relevant discrimination evidence (OR top vs bottom deciles=4.4; R²=0.029, plausibly below the h2_liability ceiling). PGS000704’s reported C-index=0.711 is a full-model time-to-event metric (not PRS-only) and its per-SD HR=1.18 suggests weaker standalone PRS signal despite huge UKB sample size and a genome-wide model; the large validation is not a reliable compensator when PRS-only performance is unreported. PGS001777 is extremely sparse (3 variants), has unknown covariates, a small evaluation sample, and a less specific phenotyping field (“Cirrhosis (males)”), increasing generalization and comparability risk. Overall, PGS004913’s endpoint-focused design plus cleaner covariate specification and stronger PRS-relevant effect evidence make it the most likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark.

PGS002237 has the strongest overall evidence package for hidden external-benchmark top rank among the shortlisted same-trait CKD scores. Its endpoint is more clinically anchored and specific (CKD stage 3+; eGFR <45), which is a key advantage for phenotype fidelity versus the broader “CKD or dialysis” definition used by PGS004158/PGS004045. While none of the candidates provide clean PRS-only AUROC/R², PGS002237 shows the strongest per-SD effect size (OR 1.47 vs ~1.39/1.38), a meaningful proxy for PRS signal strength when PRS-only metrics are absent. The very high reported AUROC=0.78 for PGS002237 is discounted because it is a covariate-heavy full model, but it still aligns with a disease-focused, multi-ancestry evaluation context that reduces transportability risk relative to the two near-clone five-biobank method-comparison scores. Between the two near-clones, PGS004158 slightly beats PGS004045, but both remain weaker than PGS002237 on endpoint fidelity and effect-size support.

PGS002072 is the best-supported choice for a hidden external benchmark given the evidence package across the shortlist. It is endpoint-faithful enough (cholelithiasis explicitly included; same composite endpoint family as PGS001861) and, in the only true near-clone comparison (PGS002072 vs PGS001861: same paper, same UKB training, same covariates, same validation context), it has both stronger structural properties (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage; 428,587 variants vs 2,059) and a slightly higher PRS signal in the same European evaluation record (partial-r 0.098 vs 0.0948). Against PGS001174, while PGS001174 has cleaner PRS-only AUROC/R2 reporting and a tighter EFO label, it comes from the sparse pan-trait UKB framework (snpnet; 970 variants) and uses a time-to-event phenotype, both of which are weaker generalization signals than the genome-wide shrinkage portability score’s construction. The pairwise judgments are internally consistent and select PGS002072 over both alternatives, and the record-level tie-break (same-context partial-r plus method/coverage) supports that outcome despite missing AUROC/R2 for PGS002072.

PGS002032 is the best-supported pick on the evidence available. It has the cleanest endpoint fidelity to the target (phenotyping/trait reported are directly “Disorders of bilirubin excretion” mapped to bilirubin metabolism disease), whereas PGS000924 is a broader composite (porphyrin + bilirubin) and time-to-event, increasing endpoint/packaging mismatch risk for a generic bilirubin-metabolism-disease benchmark. Between the two near-clone portability-paper siblings (PGS002032 vs PGS001824), the reported PRS-comparable performance is essentially identical (same partial-r=0.0716 with overlapping CIs, same cohorts/covariates/ancestry evaluation), so structural robustness becomes the tie-breaker: LDpred2 with genome-wide shrinkage and far broader variant coverage (19,768 variants) is more likely to generalize than an ultra-sparse 22-variant penalized regression score when observed performance is the same. The pairwise judgments are internally consistent in selecting PGS002032 over both alternatives, and no candidate provides cleaner, directly comparable PRS-only AUC/R² evidence that would override these endpoint and robustness advantages.

Pairwise judgments are internally consistent (PGS002755 beats both alternatives; no cycle) and grounded in multiple fields (endpoint fidelity, method/structure, effect size, validation context, covariate comparability). All three candidates map to atopic eczema, but PGS002755 and PGS004587 have the cleanest endpoint match for the generic target (incident atopic dermatitis) and are evaluated in the same large EUR cohort (n=337,910) with similar covariates, making them near-clones on phenotype/context. In that near-clone comparison, PGS002755 has materially stronger structural support for external benchmark performance (PRS-CS genome-wide shrinkage with ~1.09M variants vs 23 GWS SNPs) and a stronger reported PRS association (HR high vs low 1.249 vs 1.153), which is a legitimate tie-break when endpoints and evaluation context are effectively identical. PGS001773 is disadvantaged by endpoint mismatch (moderate-to-severe subtype), small validation (n=676), and non-comparable/likely covariate-inflated full-model metrics (AUROC 0.93, R² 0.49) that are not PRS-only and are implausible relative to the trait heritability ceiling, increasing leakage/optimism risk. Therefore PGS002755 is the best-supported choice to rank #1 in a hidden external benchmark.

All three candidates are endpoint-faithful to coronary artery disease with broadly comparable, low-leakage covariate adjustment (age/sex/PCs; PGS000013 also adds chip). The pairwise judgments are internally consistent (PGS003725 beats both alternatives; PGS002244 beats PGS000013), so the meta-decision should follow that evidence unless there is a strong record-level contradiction.

Record-level comparison supports PGS003725: it is a CAD-focused multi-ancestry PRS with broad multi-ancestry evaluation and reports materially stronger per-SD effect sizes (OR 2.14; HR 1.75) than PGS002244 (OR 1.64), which is a legitimate tie-break when PRS-only AUC/R2 are missing. PGS000013’s PRS-only R2=0.04 is clean and plausible under the heritability ceiling, but it lacks comparable effect-size evidence here and its prominent AUROC=0.81 is full-model (not PRS-only), so it should not outweigh the stronger OR/HR signal and disease-focused validation context of PGS003725.

Given the consistent pairwise wins plus the strongest available discrimination proxy (OR/HR) in a clean CAD-specific setting, PGS003725 is most likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark.

Across the three, PGS002727 has the strongest overall evidence package for hidden-benchmark top rank: it is explicitly endpoint-aligned to an asthma diagnosis context (pediatric asthma) and, unlike the two framework-style scores, comes from a disease-focused asthma PRS study. It also provides a strong PRS-discrimination signal via an OR per SD of 1.57 (a meaningful effect-size indicator when PRS-only AUC/R2 are not available), and it is supported by very large, explicitly multi-ancestry evaluation/validation (n≈391,820 with balanced ancestry strata), which reduces transportability risk. PGS001782 does offer a clean PRS-comparable metric (covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.048844), but it is evaluated only in EUR with a much smaller validation sample and comes from a broad global-biobank framework context; its evidence is narrower and less directly tied to asthma-specific optimization. PGS002061 is also a portability/framework score and reports only partial-r (0.1184) without PRS-only AUC/R2 or effect sizes, making its performance evidence less directly comparable and less compelling. The pairwise judgments are internally consistent (PGS002727 beats both alternatives), so selecting PGS002727 best matches the combined endpoint fidelity + effect-size + validation-breadth evidence.

All three candidates are endpoint-faithful for atrial fibrillation, and none reports PRS-only AUROC/R2, so we must downweight full-model discrimination and lean on covariate cleanliness, effect-size evidence, and structural/transportability signals. PGS005168’s very high C-index (0.8718) is strongly confounded by explicit clinical risk-wrapper packaging (covariates include CHARGE-AF), making its reported performance much less informative for standalone PRS ranking in an external benchmark. Between the two cleaner models, PGS005313 has a stronger structural profile (PRS-CSx, genome-wide ~1.27M variants) and broader evaluation context (multi-ancestry evaluation) than PGS002814 (P+T, 4,520 variants; EAS-only evaluation). Their per-SD effect sizes are both strong (OR 1.82 vs 1.94), so the method/coverage and validation breadth advantages are the more reliable differentiators. The pairwise judgments are internally consistent (PGS005313 beats both others, with the only moderate-confidence vote being vs PGS002814), supporting PGS005313 as most likely to rank #1 in a hidden external benchmark.

All three candidates are endpoint-faithful to abdominal aortic aneurysm, so the decision turns on comparative evidence for external PRS performance and robustness. The pairwise judgments are internally consistent (PGS003972 beats both alternatives), and their rationales are grounded in multiple fields: (i) study archetype (disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis vs portability/framework paper), (ii) model structure (genome-wide PRS-CS with ~1.12M variants vs very sparse 29-variant P+T), and (iii) metric comparability (PGS001784’s very high AUROC=0.868 is clearly full-model with heavy age/interaction covariates; its PRS-comparable signal is only modest R2=0.0147). Between the two disease-focused options, PGS003972 has the stronger structural setup for a polygenic disease (PRS-CS, genome-wide coverage, broad multi-cohort development) than PGS000753’s 29-variant score; PGS000753’s OR per SD=1.37 is only moderate and lacks PRS-only AUC/R2. Although PGS003972 reports only a full-model AUROC (0.69) with unknown covariates (so it cannot be treated as PRS-only evidence), the overall record best supports top hidden-benchmark rank among the shortlist, with lower framework/leakage risk than PGS001784 and stronger polygenic capture than PGS000753.

PGS004621 has the cleanest overall evidence package for the target endpoint (cirrhosis of liver): it is an exact endpoint match (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported both generic cirrhosis), avoiding the explicit subtype restriction of PGS000704 (alcoholic cirrhosis). Versus the other exact-match candidate PGS000726, PGS004621 is structurally more likely to rank best in an external benchmark because it is a genome-wide shrinkage PRS (PRS-CS; ~1.09M variants) rather than a 12-variant GWAS-hits score, which typically captures more distributed polygenic signal when no clean PRS-only AUC/R2 is available to arbitrate. The pairwise judgments are internally consistent (PGS004621 beats both alternatives) and grounded in endpoint fidelity plus method/variant-count considerations; the available effect-size signal (per-SD OR 1.42 for PGS004621 vs 1.32 for PGS000726; HR 1.18 for PGS000704) is directionally supportive. Full-model discrimination metrics (AUROC 0.68; C-index 0.711) are not PRS-only and are not comparable across these differing contexts, so they should not overturn the endpoint+structure advantage. Confidence remains moderate because none of the candidates reports a PRS-only AUROC/R2.

PGS001792 is the best-supported candidate for hidden external-benchmark top rank because it combines strong endpoint fidelity (primary open-angle glaucoma with matching phenotyping_reported) with the cleanest PRS-isolated performance evidence in the shortlist: a covariates-regressed-out / PGS-only Nagelkerke R2=0.03209. That PRS-only metric is directly comparable across models and is not obviously inflated relative to the provided glaucoma heritability ceiling, whereas PGS004944 reports only full-model AUROC (0.748) plus an OR and uses a self-reported endpoint (more noise), and PGS002761 provides only an OR with no AUC/R2 context and a smaller, EUR-only evaluation. The pairwise judgments are internally consistent in placing PGS001792 above both alternatives, and the record-level evidence (PRS-only R2 availability + coherent endpoint + basic covariates) supports following that consensus.

The pairwise judgments form a cycle (PGS003580 > PGS002759, PGS002759 > PGS003333, PGS003333 > PGS003580), so I re-rank from the candidate records. All three are endpoint-faithful to depressive disorder via major depressive disorder/depression mappings, and none provides a clean PRS-only AUROC/R², so structural/study-design signals dominate. PGS003333 is built with PRS-CS-auto (genome-wide shrinkage) and is developed from multiple major MDD GWAS sources (23andMe + PGC + UKB), which is a stronger robustness signal for external benchmark performance than PGS003580’s PRSice-2 thresholding with UKB-only development, and stronger than PGS002759’s limited development metadata despite having an interpretable OR (1.26 per SD, only moderate). The small full-model R² differences (0.022 vs 0.0254) are not PRS-comparable and shouldn’t drive selection; likewise, multi-ancestry evaluation listing for PGS003580 doesn’t outweigh the stronger multi-cohort disease-GWAS backing and method family of PGS003333 when the selected validation ancestry is still European. Confidence is low because covariates are unknown for PGS003333 and all candidates lack PRS-only metrics, making the decision rely on indirect evidence.

PGS001263 has the strongest endpoint fidelity to the target trait: trait_reported, trait_efo, and phenotyping_reported are all specifically “atrial flutter”, whereas PGS001339 and PGS002050 are broader atrial fibrillation+flutter composites (and PGS001339 is additionally time-to-event, a mild mismatch for a generic flutter endpoint). Among the two near-clone snpnet framework siblings (PGS001263 vs PGS001339), PGS001263 also has a small but consistent edge in PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.617 vs 0.613; PGS-only R2 0.0252 vs 0.0245) under essentially identical training/validation context and covariates, making it the better-supported flutter-specific choice. PGS002050 has a structurally stronger genome-wide LDpred2 build with many more variants, but it lacks PRS-comparable AUROC/R2 and only reports partial-r, and its endpoint is less specific; given the benchmark is for atrial flutter specifically, the direct phenotype alignment plus clean PRS-only performance evidence favors PGS001263 despite the general framework-score penalty.

I select PGS000644 as most likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark because, despite the slightly less literal phenotype label (“Nodular lymphoma” mapping to the same follicular lymphoma EFO/ICD10 concept), it has the strongest overall evidence package for a transferable PRS: a genome-wide lassosum construction with very large variant coverage (~2.2M) and multiple PRS-linked performance signals (per-SD OR 1.149; pseudo-R² reported) under clearly stated basic covariates (age/sex/batch/PCs). PGS002304 has cleaner endpoint wording (“Follicular lymphoma”) but is a 6-variant GWS score with unknown covariates and a very small validation sample (n=197); its higher full-model AUROC (0.61) is not PRS-comparable and is hard to trust as PRS-driven. Between the near-clone PRSweb siblings (PGS000644 vs PGS000643), the pairwise evidence is internally consistent that differences are small, but PGS000644 has slightly stronger discrimination/effect-size signals in the same evaluation context, making it the best-supported pick for top external performance.

PGS001783 has the strongest overall evidence package for hidden-benchmark top performance among the shortlisted same-trait COPD scores. It is an exact endpoint match (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all COPD) and, crucially, reports a clean PRS-comparable metric: covariates-regressed-out (PGS-only) Nagelkerke R2=0.038092, which is materially higher than its near-clone sibling PGS001788 (0.0163) and remains plausible under the provided COPD liability-scale heritability ceiling (~0.0388). The two PRS-CS-auto siblings share the same publication family and EUR evaluation, making this PRS-only R2 gap a legitimate tie-break. PGS004536, while COPD-aligned via ICD J44 and structurally an ensemble/metaPRS, lacks any PRS-only AUC/R2 and has unknown covariates plus explicit risk-factor integration packaging, increasing comparability/leakage risk; its lone OR=1.49 is not enough to outweigh the stronger, directly comparable PRS-only R2 evidence for PGS001783. Pairwise judgments are not fully consistent (cycle), but the most grounded near-clone comparison favors PGS001783 on the best available PRS-specific metric.

Pairwise judgments are internally consistent (PGS002763 beats both 2024 siblings; PGS004478 beats PGS004548), and the rationales rely on multiple grounded fields (endpoint clarity, covariate transparency/packaging risk, and effect-size magnitude). All three candidates align to hip osteoarthritis via trait_efo, but PGS002763 has the cleanest direct endpoint labeling (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both explicitly “Hip osteoarthritis”) and discloses a basic covariate set (age/sex/PCs/technical), reducing comparability/leakage concerns versus the Commun Biol ‘risk factor PRS + disease PRS integration’ family where covariates are unknown. The pairwise judgments are internally consistent (PGS005217 beats both others; PGS002055 beats PGS001843), and their rationales are grounded in endpoint fidelity, study archetype, and available performance/effect-size evidence, so selecting PGS005217 is best supported. Confidence remains moderate because none of the candidates report clean PGS-only AUROC/R2, and PGS005217’s reported C-index is a full-model metric rather than a directly comparable PRS-only measure.

Pairwise judgments are internally consistent (PGS005235 beats both alternatives), and the underlying record supports that outcome on the highest-weight factors. Endpoint fidelity is strongest for PGS005235 because its phenotyping_reported is an explicit obesity diagnosis (phecode 278.1) rather than a broad administrative bundle (PGS002033) or a time-to-event construct (PGS001298). On performance evidence, while PGS005235 lacks PRS-comparable AUROC/R², it reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR≈1.97), which is a meaningful discriminator signal and materially stronger than PGS002033’s modest partial correlation (partial-r≈0.079) and more compelling than PGS001298’s modest PRS-only AUROC/R² (AUROC≈0.576; R²≈0.011) given PGS001298’s pan-trait sparse-framework archetype and TTE endpoint. Structurally, PGS005235 uses genome-wide shrinkage (LDpred2-auto) with large variant coverage and is developed from multi-cohort GWAS sources (EGG/GIANT/UKB), reducing single-biobank framework risk relative to the UKB portability/framework candidates. Missing AUROC/R² keeps confidence at Moderate, but the combined endpoint alignment + strong OR + study archetype make it the most likely hidden-benchmark #1.

PGS000923 has the strongest overall evidence package for the target trait sarcoidosis: it is the only candidate with direct concept alignment (trait_efo="sarcoidosis" and phenotyping_reported explicitly "TTE sarcoidosis") and it reports clean PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.6456; PGS-only R2=0.018) under basic covariates, with R2 plausibly below the provided heritability ceiling. The pairwise judgments are internally consistent and also favor PGS000923 over both alternatives, supporting this selection.

PGS000903 is the best-supported candidate to rank #1 on an external PD benchmark because it is endpoint-faithful (Parkinson’s disease across trait/phenotype fields) and comes from the same strong, disease-focused Lancet Neurol GWAS meta-analysis family as PGS000902, but with a materially richer polygenic construction (C+T, 1,805 variants vs 90 GWAS hits). PGS004155 is the strongest choice given the evidence and the pairwise judgments. The margins are small and based on full-model metrics (no PGS-only AUC/R² available), so confidence remains moderate.

All three candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match carcinoma in situ of skin), study family (same publication), cohort/archetype (MGI), ancestry (EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL), covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), and sample sizes (training n=6,005; validation n=5,500). Across the shortlist, PGS005219 and PGS005220 are the most endpoint-faithful to the target (sleep apnea) via a coherent obstructive sleep apnea diagnosis phenotype, and both come from the same disease-focused multi-cohort development context (FinnGen/MGBB/MVP) with the same evaluation setting (same covariates including BMI, same validation N, same reported full-model AUROC). Between the near-clone siblings PGS005219 vs PGS005220, the only meaningful differentiator in the visible record is PRS signal strength: PGS005219 shows a materially larger per-SD OR (1.98 vs 1.53) under otherwise matched design, which is legitimate tie-break evidence when PRS-only AUC/R2 are absent. Pairwise judgments are internally consistent (PGS005219 beats both others), supporting selection of PGS005219.

PGS002040 is the best-supported pick for hidden-benchmark top rank because it wins the only clean near-clone comparison available: against PGS001833 it matches endpoint/phenotyping, cohort, covariates, and evaluation context, yet shows higher PRS-comparable signal (partial-r 0.0276 vs 0.0218). Pairwise judgments are mostly consistent in pointing to PGS002040 as the overall winner, with the only dissent being PGS001137 over PGS001833, which does not overturn the stronger near-clone win of PGS002040.

All three candidates are endpoint-faithful near-clones (same squamous cell carcinoma phenotype, same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL context, same MGI training/validation sizes, and same basic covariates), and none reports PRS-only AUROC/R²—so we must rely on within-family tie-breakers (effect sizes and the limited, covariate-influenced full-model metrics). All three candidates are near-clones from the same publication with identical endpoint fidelity (schizophrenia across trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported), identical method family (PRS-CS), identical evaluation ancestry (EUR), and similarly basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/platform/batch). Thus, the most defensible pick for likely #1 hidden-benchmark rank is the original, coherently supported score PGS000083.

Given the consistent pairwise wins and the combination of disease-focused design + strong effect-size signal + genome-wide coverage, PGS002726 is the most likely to rank #1 in an external MS PGS benchmark.
